notes.title: ✨ The 1.0 Update ✨
notes.notes:
It's been fun working on Toilet Spiders, and I'm excited to bring the game out of Early Access with the 1.0 Update! Thank you everyone who's played and provided feedback. Here is what's new in Version 1.0:


 Randomized Scripted Scare Moments: The spiders have escaped their toilets... Players have requested more life to the facility in between bathrooms, so as of v1.0, you may now encounter unexpected events during your playthrough. Keep your eyes peeled...
 Along with the controller vibration that was added in the last update, there is now DualShock 4/DualSense controller light support on desktop! If you have a PlayStation controller handy, give it a go.
 "Resource Peek" ability added! I got tired of having to pause the game to check my light bulb/flashbang count when entering a bathroom, so now you can hold R1/Tab at any time to "peek" at what you have in your pockets.
 Super rare spider kill variant, by request (of a five-year-old.) Exactly one out of the 100 spiders present in the facility has now learned karate.
 Commentary Mode! Like all Fullbright games, Toilet Spiders now has a dedicated Commentary Mode. Just toggle it on in the options and a selection of Commentary icons will appear throughout the facility. Activating them will give you a little insight into the inspirations for the game, how it was made, how it works under the hood, and other little bits and bobs! It was fun to make and I hope you'll enjoy learning a little bit more about where the game came from. I mean, Half-Life 2 just did it, why not us? Oh, and there's a new Achievement for finding all the Commentary nodes in one run as well.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45259513/df8ac0e3af0553c285321831a62f0222db94d565.jpg

Bugfixes and tweaks:

 Fixed a visual gap in the floor in the storage room behind Barracks, a couple of places where the player's view could get inside an occluder volume.
 Fixed one or more instances where controller vibration could continue when it wasn't supposed to.
 Improved a couple instances of frame hitches on interact.
 Improved visual appearance of volumetric lights.
 Fixed issue where vertical look sensitivity was scaled down too much compared to horizontal when using mouse.
 Fixed issue where player couldn't pause or interact while "Volunteers Remaining" text appeared onscreen.
 Ensuring menu flow on backing out of restart confirmation screen works as intended in all cases.
 Fixed an issue where if you died/restarted while standing in the Courtyard, main camera's clear flag would be set improperly.
 Fixed issue where you could hear the audio fade up twice in a row when restarting in certain situations.

OK, from this point forward Toilet Spiders will be in maintenance mode-- so if you run into any major bugs, let me know in the Steam discussion forums. And if any new translation languages come in, I'll add those in an update as well! (If you'd like to do a translation into your language and be credited in the game, take a look in the Steam discussion forum for instructions.)

Alright, thank you Volunteers-- and good luck!

notes.title: Hotfix: stuck bug
notes.notes:
Hotfix for a stuck bug that was discovered in the barracks-- no, not a spider that was stuck, but a place the player could get stuck, if they tried to climb inside the footlocker trunk that has its lid busted off and leaning there like a little ramp. You used to be able to climb in there and then you couldn't get out; now you can't get in at all.

Please, the footlockers are not a jungle gym.

notes.title: Patch notes: the vibes update
notes.notes:
Patch notes to go along with Update #3:


 Controller rumble support added throughout. User can toggle vibration in Options.
 Performance improvements to bring perf back up to 60fps on Steam Deck
 Fix for a rare softlock that was introduced on Lucky Coin pickup
 A couple of other minor fixes and presentation tweaks

notes.title: Update #3
notes.notes:
The VIBES UPDATE is here! As you may have guessed, the big addition is full controller vibration support throughout the game. Now when your geiger counter goes off you'll feel it rumble in your hands, along with rumble feedback for other interactions and scripted moments. Controller rumble support is a first for a Fullbright game! It was fun to get figured out and get working and wired up throughout the game. Rumble is best experienced with a controller on desktop, or via an external controller on Steam Deck-- I've found that the internal Steam Deck controller rumble support is really.. let's say, subtle, though it is there. And if you're not a fan, you can toggle it off in the options. If you encounter any issues with the rumble feature (or anything else) click on over to the Steam Discussions board and let me know!

Speaking of Steam Deck, I also found that after a recent OS update, it seemed like performance had degraded by 5-10 fps throughout the game (and across a variety of other games on Deck, in my testing.) My first blush reaction was kind of like, well, it's an OS update, what can you do-- but, regardless of the cause, it made the experience of playing the game on Deck slightly worse for users... so I found a way to gain back a good amount of performance, and so with this update the game is back up to a solid 60fps throughout the experience (with the occasional single-frame blip into the 57/58-ish fps range, depending on what the player is doing.) And those performance gains will translate to desktop/laptop as well-- so enjoy your frames!

In the prior update I also managed to introduce a very rare soft lock that could happen when picking up a Lucky Coin. That is now fixed-- or so I believe!! Again, if you run into any crashes, hangs, soft locks or other stuck spots, just throw a post in the Discussions forum.

Alright, probably just a couple more updates like this before we hit 1.0 on this thing... thanks, and good luck!

notes.title: Update #2: New Intro & Ending, plus other neat stuff
notes.notes:
Fullbright Presents TOILET SPIDERS Early Access Update #2 is HERE! After last patch's usability and QoL focus, this time around I'm leaning into more story-based requests I've seen from the community. To this end, the game now kicks off with an intro sequence setting the stage for your Volunteer mission. And if you're able to successfully escape, stick around after the credits for an ending sequence that wraps up your victory!

There are also two paper "You-Are-Here"-style maps posted up in the corridors of the game, one for each "floor" of the facility. You can refer to these in the main connecting hallway of each of the two major areas, adding both some useful info and a little bit of fictional flavor to your mission.

There's also a little flower to find. It doesn't do much, but it's cute.

Also there's a new note somewhere in the depths of the facility, and the Investigator Achievement has been updated to include it, if you haven't picked that one up yet. And you may notice something a little different about your geiger counter when you recover it after one of your Volunteers dies...

The game's first Fan Translation is also included: Turkish, by Mutlu "Y.J. Malmsteen" Koksal! It's really exciting to see the game in new languages. If you'd like to submit a fan translation and be credited in a future version of the game, head to the Steam forum  for instructions on how to get your language into TOILET SPIDERS!

Alright, good luck, have fun!

-steve

notes.title: Update #1: Restart Your Run (and other quality of life options)
notes.notes:
It's been less than a week since TOILET SPIDERS invaded your innocent computer, and the first update is now available! Everything in this update is based on player feedback, so THANK YOU for your input, those who have tried out the initial Early Access version!

As TOILET SPIDERS is a run-based game with some amount of RNG involved, one request was a way to restart the game without quitting and relaunching-- so now, we've got that! Just choose Restart from the main menu and you'll start a new run with spider locations and placement of resources re-randomized.

There are also a number of new user options, especially targeted at players with motion sickness: you can now up the field of view even further, turn off view bobbing while walking/running, enable a reticle in the center of the screen, and more.

Also to accommodate folks who can't stand that ringing-in-the-ears sound following a flashbang, and who are sensitive to sudden screen flashes, there is now a "Gentle Flashbangs" option which tones down the flash effect and removes the tinnitus sound, as well as toning down the explosion sound in general.

The next update will be more content-focused (and probably take longer.) I hope you'll make good use of these new options til then. Thanks for your patience, and thanks for playing!
